subject: Re: [stan-users] Clarification on Change of Variables

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Clarification on Change of Variables
parts:
Stan only applies Jacobians for implicit transformations
due to constraints on parameters. Everything else is up to
the user.

It's when the parameters are on the left of the sampling
statements, at least under the usual interpretation of sampling
notation, that you need to add the log Jacobian determinant.

The normal example you provide is subtle because the density
normal(y|mu,sigma) is equivalent to normal(mu|y,sigma). So
the contribution to the log probability is the same in Stan for

mu1 * mu2 ~ normal(y, sigma);

and

y ~ normal(mu1 * mu2, sigma);

But the modeling implication is usually different, with the
former notation implying a Jacobian is required under the
usual interpretation and the latter not requiring it.

- Bob


On Aug 12, 2014, at 12:50 AM, Soga Shota <soga....@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi all,
>
> I want to clarify the change of variables and when to increment log probability, especially what is meant by linear transformation in the manual.
>
> In the stan manual, it says we do need to increment log probability with "non-linear transformation."
>
> I thought a linear transformation is defined as: new_param = const0 + const1*param1 + const2*param2 + ... + constN*paramN
> and I thought this is not linear transformation: new_param = param1*param2*...*paramN
>
> but I saw an example that uses the second transformation without Jacobian adjustment. Here is my simple example:
>
> parameters
> {
> real mu_a;
> real mu_b;
> real<lower=0,upper=1> sigma;
> real y;
> }
> model
> {
> mu_a ~ normal(0,1);
> mu_b ~ normal(0,1);
> y ~ normal(mu_a*mu_b,sigma);
> }
>
> I thought that I have to adjust Jacobian for mu_a*mu_b, but many examples don't.
>
> Is it correct to understand that stan automatically handles any transformation consists of multiplications?
>
> Thank you for your attention.
>
> Shota
